title: Problem
body_md:
Let $\mathcal{D}_n$ be the set of words with $n$ letters $N$ and $n$ letters $E$ such that every prefix contains at least as many $N$'s as $E$'s.\footnote{This is the definition of Dyck paths as in Section~\ref{sec:qt-combinatorics}.} For $D\in\mathcal{D}_n$, let $a(D)$ be the length of its initial run of $N$'s and $b(D)$ the length of its terminal run of $E$'s, with both equal to zero for the empty path. Construct a uniform, combinatorially meaningful bijection $\phi:\mathcal{D}_n\to\mathcal{D}_n$ satisfying
\[
a(\phi(D))=b(D),\qquad b(\phi(D))=a(D).
\]
Supply mutually inverse Python functions \texttt{forward(path)} and \texttt{inverse(path)}, and explain the map through the structure of paths. Such a map explains the symmetry of the polynomials $F_n(q,t)=\sum_{D\in\mathcal{D}_n}q^{a(D)}t^{b(D)}$.
head: manual

title: Counterexamples
body_md:
The three counterexamples are about the target polynomials themselves, not about
candidate statistics. In each case, the target polynomial has a negative coefficient outside the
evaluated parameter range: for Problem~9, the coefficient of $q^1t^0$ at tier sizes $(10,9,9)$ is
$-2{,}871{,}205{,}236{,}900$; for Problem~10, the constant term at $n=7$,
$k=2$ is $-8{,}484$; and for Problem~11, the constant term at
$(m,n,k)=(2,11,1)$ is $-528$. The generating function of a statistic has
nonnegative coefficients, so no statistic can generate these polynomials. These counterexamples are of considerable value to algebraic combinatorics community.
